summary: Flora Valley Airport is a small remote airstrip located in the Kimberley region of Western Australia, serving the surrounding pastoral and Aboriginal communities. The airport primarily supports fly-in fly-out (FIFO) mining operations, cattle station access, and essential regional air services. Its isolation in the rugged outback makes it a vital lifeline for travelers and workers in this sparsely populated part of Australia.
faqs:
Q: What is Flora Valley Airport primarily used for?
A: It mainly serves remote pastoral stations, mining operations, and occasional charter flights in the Kimberley region.

Q: Are there scheduled commercial flights to Flora Valley Airport?
A: No, the airport is not served by regular scheduled airlines; flights are typically chartered for specific operational or community needs.

Q: What facilities are available at Flora Valley Airport?
A: As a small outback airstrip, facilities are minimal, typically limited to a basic runway, parking area, and no terminal buildings.

Q: What is the best time of year to fly into Flora Valley?
A: The dry season (May to September) is generally preferred due to more predictable weather and better visibility in the Kimberley region.
transport_tips: Ground transport options at Flora Valley Airport are extremely limited, so passengers should arrange transfers in advance through their host station, mine site, or charter operator. Most travelers fly in as part of organized work rotations or station visits, with pickup typically pre-arranged. The nearest major town with road access is several hours away, so plan fuel and supplies accordingly.
local_tip: Carry extra drinking water and sun protection even for short stops on the tarmac — the Kimberley sun is intense year-round, and shaded areas at remote strips are nonexistent.
